descriptive_title: Grade 3 Mathematics: Demonstrations — Perimeter, Area, Capacity, Mass, and Time (E2.1-E2.9)
subject: Mathematics

curriculum_expectations.E2.1: use appropriate units of length to estimate, measure, and compare the perimeters of polygons and curved shapes, and construct polygons with a given perimeter
curriculum_expectations.E2.2: explain the relationships between millimetres, centimetres, metres, and kilometres as metric units of length, and use benchmarks for these units to estimate lengths
curriculum_expectations.E2.3: use non-standard units appropriately to estimate, measure, and compare capacity, and explain the effect that overfilling or underfilling, and gaps between units, have on accuracy
curriculum_expectations.E2.4: compare, estimate, and measure the mass of various objects, using a pan balance and non-standard units
curriculum_expectations.E2.5: use various units of different sizes to measure the same attribute of a given item, and demonstrate that even though using different-sized units produces a different count, the size of the attribute remains the same
curriculum_expectations.E2.6: use analog and digital clocks and timers to tell time in hours, minutes, and seconds
curriculum_expectations.E2.7: compare the areas of two-dimensional shapes by matching, covering, or decomposing and recomposing the shapes, and demonstrate that different shapes can have the same area
curriculum_expectations.E2.8: use appropriate non-standard units to measure area, and explain the effect that gaps and overlaps have on accuracy
curriculum_expectations.E2.9: use square centimetres (cm2) and square metres (m2) to estimate, measure, and compare the areas of various two-dimensional shapes, including those with curved sides

unit_overview: A 5-day Grade 3 unit on measurement (E2.1-E2.9) framed around 'Fencing the Farm' — Roo the Ruler Rabbit and Cal the Calendar Cat help Farmer Phil. Day 1 measures PERIMETER with mm, cm, m, km benchmarks. Day 2 compares AREAS by matching and covering. Day 3 introduces SQUARE CM and SQUARE M for area. Day 4 measures CAPACITY and MASS with non-standard units, showing same-attribute different-counts. Day 5 closes with TIME (analog + digital) and a Big Farm Capstone. Each lesson includes an expanded_walkthrough.
unit_learning_goal: Children will measure perimeter, area, capacity, mass, and time using appropriate units and tools.

lesson_arc.big_idea: PERIMETER is the distance AROUND a shape. Measure with mm, cm, m, or km depending on size.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can measure perimeter and pick the right metric unit.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Roo fences 4 polygons; children measure perimeter and pick units.

lesson_arc.big_idea: AREA is the SPACE INSIDE a shape. Compare by MATCHING, COVERING, or DECOMPOSING.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can compare areas of shapes by matching or covering.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Roo covers shapes with tiles; children compare 4 shape pairs.

lesson_arc.big_idea: AREA is measured in SQUARE UNITS — cm² for small, m² for big.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can measure area in square centimetres and square metres.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Roo counts cm² grids; children measure 6 shapes in cm² or m².

lesson_arc.big_idea: CAPACITY is HOW MUCH it holds. MASS is HOW HEAVY. Different unit sizes = different counts, same attribute.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can measure capacity and mass with non-standard units.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Cal pours and weighs; children compare cups vs scoops, big rocks vs small.

lesson_arc.big_idea: TELL TIME in hours, minutes, seconds. Use the right TOOL for each job.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can tell time and pick the right measurement tool.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Children rotate 4 stations: perimeter, area, capacity/mass, time.

recurring_characters.name: Roo the Ruler Rabbit
recurring_characters.role: Lead character. Same Roo from G1/G2 measurement; now adds perimeter and area. Anchors all 5 lessons.
recurring_characters.visual_description: A young rabbit with long ears, holding a colourful ruler and measuring tape.

recurring_characters.name: Cal the Calendar Cat
recurring_characters.role: Roo's partner. Time + capacity character. Cameo Lessons 4-5.
recurring_characters.visual_description: A small striped cat with a wall calendar over its shoulder, holding a stopwatch.

threaded_vocabulary.child_friendly_definition: The distance AROUND a shape. Add up all sides.
The SPACE INSIDE a shape. Cover it with squares.
Tiny unit. 1 mm = a pinhead. 10 mm = 1 cm.
Big unit. 1 km = 1000 m. About 12 minutes walking.
1 cm × 1 cm square. Used for small areas.
1 m × 1 m square. Used for big areas.
A very short time. 1 second = 'one Mississippi'.

pedagogical_notes: Grade 3 expands G2 measurement to perimeter, area, capacity, mass, and time.
9 expectations packed into 5 days — focus on big ideas, not mastery of all.
Perimeter = around. Area = inside. Use both terms explicitly.
Same-attribute different-counts is core to E2.5 — drive it home with cup vs scoop.
Time uses BOTH analog and digital — show both forms.
canadian_context_notes: Canadian farm context: Ontario dairy farm.
Hockey rink area as ~1500 m² benchmark.
Tim Hortons cup volume for capacity.
School yard perimeter for km estimation.
